item.title: CIMIC’s Leighton Asia to acquire Malaysia’s LWE, expanding cleanroom capabilities
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Leighton Asia, under Australia-based CIMIC Group, will acquire Malaysian mechanical, electrical, and plumbing services company LWE and its cleanroom business CLIN.
item.content:encoded:
Leighton Asia, under Australia-based CIMIC Group, will acquire Malaysian mechanical, electrical, and plumbing services company LWE and its cleanroom business CLIN.

In a statement on Monday, HOCHTIEF, the parent firm of CIMIC, said the deal can strengthen Leighton Asia’s end-to-end capabilities in advanced technology. The company did not provide any details about finance or timeline.

The acquisition will enhance Leighton Asia’s offering for clients in high-growth sectors including semiconductors, pharmaceuticals, healthcare, data centers, renewable energy, and industrial development. It will also add in-house MEP capability and established cleanroom fabrication capacity in Penang, Malaysia.

ACS Group and HOCHTIEF CEO and CIMIC Group Executive Chairman Juan Santamaría said “The acquisition of LWE and CLIN is aligned with our strategy to expand our capabilities in advanced technology and provide clients with more integrated, end-to-end solutions.”

“LWE and CLIN bring specialist expertise, established client relationships and more than four decades of experience. Combined with Leighton Asia’s regional presence and project delivery capability, this positions us to capture new opportunities in advanced technology and cleanroom markets across Asia, Australia and Europe,” the executive added.

Leighton Asia Managing Director Jan Torka said “LWE’s MEP expertise and CLIN’s cleanroom capabilities are a strong complement to our business. Cleanrooms are a critical component of advanced technology, semiconductor and pharmaceutical projects, and this acquisition significantly strengthens our position in these growing sectors.”

item.title: Votee AI partners AI Singapore to explore AI research for Southeast Asian languages
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: Votee AI and AI Singapore (AISG) have signed a memorandum of understanding to explore research and development on large language models for Southeast Asian languages, with initial focus areas to be jointly prioritized.
item.content:encoded:
Votee AI and AI Singapore (AISG) have signed a memorandum of understanding to explore research and development on large language models for Southeast Asian languages, with initial focus areas to be jointly prioritized.

Under the MoU, the organizations intend to explore joint research, the exchange of technical know-how, shared evaluation benchmarks and co-authored publications, the duo said in a statement on last Friday.

The work is at an exploratory stage, with initial language priorities to be jointly discussed.

It is noted that more than 600 million people live in Southeast Asia, while many languages in the region remain underserved by global AI models.

The proposed work will explore models built with regional data and evaluated against regional benchmarks.

Votee AI aims to bring what it has learned building Cantonese language AI to other underserved languages.

Its engineering team includes developers based in Ho Chi Minh City, and the company plans to draw on them as the work extends to Southeast Asian languages.

“Asia Pacific is one of the fastest-growing markets for generative AI, yet language competency in low-resource languages remains a barrier to broader adoption. Through our MoU with AI Singapore, we look forward to exploring regional language-model research that can help bridge this divide and support AI adoption by governments and enterprises,

“Our experience developing Cantonese language AI and supporting its adoption gives us a strong foundation to contribute to this work with like-minded institutions such as AI Singapore,” said Pak-Sun Ting, Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer of Votee AI.

Leslie Teo, Senior Director of AI Products, AI Singapore said that advancing AI for Southeast Asia requires collaboration across the ecosystem.

He said the exploration of joint research and shared evaluation benchmarks can raise the quality and reliability of language models for the region.

Jacky Chan, Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer of Votee AI, also said the firm’s approach is consistent: rigorous benchmarks first, open research where possible, and models institutions can own and run on their own infrastructure.

“We co-authored HKCanto-Eval (CoNLL 2025) for Cantonese. We want Southeast Asian languages to have the same scientific foundation,” he added.

item.title: China’s MegaRobo raises nearly $200M for AI lab automation
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: China's MegaRobo Technologies has raised nearly $200 million to expand AI-connected laboratory automation and physical-world intelligence systems.
item.content:encoded:
China-based MegaRobo Technologies has raised nearly $200 million in a financing round to expand artificial intelligence systems that connect models and software with laboratory instruments, robotics and other physical equipment.

Oman Investment Authority, the sovereign wealth fund of Oman, joined the round, while existing investors Asia Investment Capital, Granite Asia and Sinovation Ventures continued their backing. CMB International also participated as a new investor, according to MegaRobo’s November 18 announcement.

The company did not identify a lead investor, disclose a valuation or assign a formal stage to the round. It said it has raised approximately $600 million across multiple financing rounds, including a nearly $300 million Series C co-led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Asia Investment Capital and Granite Asia.

MegaRobo said the new capital will support core technology development, international expansion of its AI-for-science business and infrastructure that allows AI systems to operate across complex physical environments.

The company develops what it calls the One Intelligence Stack, which combines models and agents, data, workflows, scientific instruments and automation in one system. In laboratory use, the architecture is intended to let software design experiments, send instructions to robotic equipment, capture results and use the resulting data to guide subsequent work.

The platform is organized around a cycle of designing, executing, observing and learning from physical experiments. MegaRobo presents science as the first application because laboratory work requires software to move beyond analyzing digital information and interact directly with instruments, samples and changing experimental conditions.

The financing has direct regional relevance because MegaRobo is headquartered in China and plans to expand its operations across Asia as well as North America, Europe and the Middle East. Its systems also address pharmaceutical research and advanced manufacturing, including workflows in semiconductors and display production.

MegaRobo has delivered scientific-intelligence infrastructure to more than 500 pharmaceutical companies, biotechnology businesses, contract research organizations and research institutions. The company’s automated laboratory service has worked with more than 200 customers. Those operating figures originate from the company and have not been independently audited.

MegaRobo was founded in 2016. Earlier investors include WuXi AppTec and Bosch Ventures, while Pavilion Capital, part of Temasek’s Seviora Group, participated in the company’s previous Series C financing.

The company said it will use its technology beyond life sciences in physical systems that require AI to interact with instruments, machines, materials and production processes. It did not provide a deployment timetable, new customer commitments or a geographic breakdown for the expansion funded by the new round.

MEGAROBO Unveils High-Content Cell Imaging System for Advanced Multidimensional Biological Analysis

item.title: Vietnam-France-Korea consortium wins $423M design contract for Vietnam’s $67B high-speed railway
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: A consortium of firms from Vietnam, South Korea, and France has won a feasibility study and basic design contract for Vietnam's North-South high-speed railway, worth KRW560 billion ($423 million), South Korea's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport said.
item.content:encoded:
A consortium of firms from Vietnam, South Korea, and France has won a feasibility study and basic design contract for Vietnam’s North-South high-speed railway, worth KRW560 billion ($423 million), South Korea’s Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport said.

In a statement on Sunday, the ministry said the contract was awarded on November 21. The consortium includes Korea Rail Network Authority (KNR), Samboo Engineering, and Yooshin Engineering from South Korea; France’s SYSTRA; and Vietnam’s Transport Engineering Design Incorporated (TEDI). The ministry said more than 40 rail design firms competed for the work.

The consortium will carry out the study and design over 30 months, from November 2026 to May 2029. The feasibility study is scheduled for 18 months and the basic design for 12 months.

The ministry emphasized the award as the largest overseas rail planning and design contract for South Korea. It credited the government’s support, including two summits between the leaders of Korea and Vietnam, in August 2025 and April 2026, and ministerial delegations in June and July 2026. A presidential letter was also delivered, the ministry added.

The full project would build a double-track high-speed line of about 1,541 kilometers from Hanoi to Ho Chi Minh City, designed for speeds of 350 kilometers per hour. It would have four sections: Hanoi to Vinh (281 kilometers), Vinh to Da Nang (420 kilometers), Da Nang to Nha Trang (480 kilometers) and Nha Trang to Ho Chi Minh City (360 kilometers).

The ministry said construction is due to start in 2029 and the line to open in 2035. The total project cost is $67.3 billion.

item.title: GlobalFoundries invests $10M in India’s Cyient Semiconductors
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: GlobalFoundries has approved a $10 million strategic investment in Hyderabad-based Cyient Semiconductors, subject to definitive agreements and customary conditions.
item.content:encoded:
GlobalFoundries has approved a $10 million strategic equity investment in Hyderabad-based Cyient Semiconductors, adding capital and a manufacturing relationship to India’s growing custom-chip design ecosystem.

Cyient Semiconductors said the proposed investment values the company at $490 million before the transaction and $510 million after it, including its recent financing from Edelweiss. The investment remains subject to the execution of definitive transaction documents and other customary conditions.

An exchange filing by parent company Cyient said GlobalFoundries U.S. would subscribe to fully and compulsorily convertible cumulative preference shares for the rupee equivalent of $10 million under a proposed share subscription and shareholders’ agreement.

Cyient Semiconductors said it plans to use the proceeds to expand its turnkey custom application-specific integrated circuit services, accelerate custom-silicon programs and improve wafer-supply assurance. The company provides chip design and development services from specification through production and works with customers in industrial, automotive, communications and other markets.

Its end-to-end work spans chip architecture, design, manufacturing coordination, packaging, testing, qualification and supply-chain management, according to the filing. The company focuses on analog mixed-signal, intelligent-power and advanced semiconductor platforms, with design centers in India, Belgium and the United States. It serves customers in data centers, robotics, automotive, industrial automation, communications and health care.

The investment follows Cyient Semiconductors’ recent strategic financing from Edelweiss. That transaction was announced at the same $490 million pre-money equity valuation. The new capital would bring the combined post-money valuation to $510 million, according to the company.

GlobalFoundries operates semiconductor manufacturing facilities in the United States, Europe and Singapore. The companies said the relationship is intended to combine Cyient Semiconductors’ custom-chip design capabilities with GlobalFoundries’ manufacturing platform and supply capacity.

Cyient Semiconductors CEO Suman Narayan said the investment would support engineering capabilities and global customer engagements while improving access to manufacturing. Those operational benefits are the company’s stated plans and depend on the transaction and subsequent execution.

For India, the proposed transaction adds an international foundry partner to a locally based semiconductor design business as public and private investment expands across the country’s chip value chain. Cyient Semiconductors is headquartered in Hyderabad and operates as part of engineering and technology company Cyient.

Cyient Semiconductors attributed its funding, valuation and expansion plans to the announced transaction. Neither the company release nor the exchange filing disclosed a timetable for completing the investment. The parties must finalize the transaction documents before the subscription is completed.

Cyient Semiconductors Announces Strategic Financing with Edelweiss at ~ USD 500 Mn. Equity Valuation

item.title: PayerMax, ShopeePay to expand partnership in digital payments, merchant services
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: PayerMax and ShopeePay will deepen their existing partnership and explore further opportunities in digital payments and merchant services, as the two have signed a memorandum of understanding at the 2026 Singapore FinTech Festival.
item.content:encoded:
PayerMax and ShopeePay will deepen their existing partnership and explore further opportunities in digital payments and merchant services, as the two have signed a memorandum of understanding at the 2026 Singapore FinTech Festival.

In a statement last Saturday, PayerMax said the signing was attended by Teddy Setiawan Tee, Regional Director, Indonesia at PayerMax, and Lala Eka Nilam, President Director of ShopeePay Indonesia.

Building on their existing payment collaboration, both companies aim to expand payment acceptance capabilities for merchants and explore new opportunities to connect international businesses with local payment ecosystems. The partnership reflects their shared commitment to enhancing payment experiences, addressing diverse consumer preferences, and supporting the continued development of digital commerce across Southeast Asia.

Building on Existing Payment Collaboration

Southeast Asia, especially Indonesia remains an important market for PayerMax, with diverse payment ecosystems and distinct consumer preferences across countries. For international businesses entering or expanding in the region, offering familiar local payment methods is essential to delivering convenient and seamless payment experiences.

PayerMax and ShopeePay have already established a strong foundation for collaboration in local digital payments.

In Malaysia, for example, PayerMax enables eligible merchants to offer ShopeePay as a payment option through their existing checkout integration, supporting both wallet balance payments and SPayLater for eligible consumers. This allows merchants in gaming, digital entertainment, and other online service sectors to provide more flexible payment choices while simplifying local payment integration and management.

Beyond payment acceptance, both teams have also worked closely on payment-related fund flows and reconciliation processes, establishing clear operational procedures that support transparency and confidence in their collaboration.

Together, these efforts demonstrate how closer collaboration between payment service providers can help international merchants address practical payment needs, streamline operations, and deliver more convenient payment experiences to local consumers.

Exploring Further Opportunities in Digital Payments and Merchant Services:

Under the MOU, PayerMax and ShopeePay will explore collaboration in the following areas:

Digital Payment Collaboration: Exploring opportunities to strengthen existing cooperation in digital payment services to address evolving merchant and consumer payment needs.

Merchant Payment Solutions: Exploring opportunities to provide international merchants with more locally relevant payment choices and support diverse digital commerce scenarios.

Merchant Growth and Engagement: Exploring localized marketing initiatives and smoother payment experiences to help merchants reach more consumers, encourage repeat purchases, and support transaction growth.

Through these initiatives, both companies aim to build on their existing partnership, combining payment capabilities and local market expertise to support the evolving needs of businesses operating across Southeast Asian markets.

Supporting the Growth of Digital Commerce in Southeast Asia

As digital commerce continues to evolve, merchants increasingly need payment solutions that accommodate different consumer behaviors, transaction preferences, and business models.

From gaming and digital entertainment to e-commerce and online services, providing suitable local payment options can help businesses create more accessible payment experiences and better serve consumers in different markets.

By deepening their existing partnership, PayerMax and ShopeePay look forward to identifying further opportunities to enhance local payment experiences, strengthen merchant engagement, and support international businesses as they expand across the region.

Teddy Setiawan Tee, Regional Director, Indonesia at PayerMax, said “Southeast Asia is a dynamic digital payment market, where understanding local payment preferences is essential for international businesses. At PayerMax, we believe that strong local partnerships play a key role in helping merchants navigate different markets. We look forward to strengthening our collaboration with ShopeePay and exploring opportunities that can better serve merchants and consumers across the region.”

Lala Eka Nilam, President Director of ShopeePay Indonesia, said “Our partnership with PayerMax has helped connect ShopeePay Indonesia with merchants beyond Southeast Asia, supported by close collaboration on payment acceptance, fund flows, and reconciliation. This strong operational foundation has enabled us to better serve both merchants and consumers.”

“Looking ahead, we see opportunities to combine PayerMax’s merchant connections with ShopeePay’s understanding of Indonesian consumers and campaign expertise to explore more relevant marketing initiatives and smoother payment experiences. Together, we aim to help merchants attract and retain customers, drive transaction growth, and contribute to greater digital financial inclusion in Indonesia,” he added

Through this MOU, PayerMax and ShopeePay reaffirm their commitment to building on their existing collaboration, leveraging their complementary capabilities to explore new opportunities for merchants and consumers across Southeast Asia.

item.title: Canadia Impact Fund, Plug and Play APAC to jointly connect Cambodia startups to global stage
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Canadia Impact Fund, an investment fund based in Cambodia, and Plug and Play APAC, a Southeast Asia-focused venture capital, will jointly connect Cambodian start-ups with international networks, expertise and investment opportunities.
item.content:encoded:
Canadia Impact Fund, an investment fund based in Cambodia, and Plug and Play APAC, a Southeast Asia-focused venture capital, will jointly connect Cambodian start-ups with international networks, expertise and investment opportunities.

The two sides have signed signed a memorandum of understanding for the cooperation, at FrancoTech 2026, held at Koh Pich Expo in Cambodia, on the sidelines of the 20th Francophonie Summit. The MoU sets a framework for collaboration to connect Cambodian start-ups with international networks, expertise, and investment opportunities.

From Silicon Valley to Singapore: a global innovation network

Founded in Silicon Valley, Plug and Play is an innovation platform that connects start-ups, corporations, investors and institutions through accelerator programs and corporate innovation activities. With a worldwide presence in more than 30 countries and 60 locations, the APAC operations are based in Singapore, where Plug and Play APAC works with start-ups and stakeholders across the region.

Building the next chapter of Cambodia’s start-up ecosystem

FrancoTech was the moment to formalize a relationship that had already begun. In 2025, the Ministry of Post and Telecommunications (MPTC) brought the Plug and Play accelerator to Cambodia. At the launch of Plug and Play Cambodia, Thierry Tea, Co-Founder of CIFC, met Mike Maceda of Plug and Play APAC and So Visoty, Secretary of State at MPTC in charge of start-up development. Together, they discussed how to work together and build a stronger innovation and tech ecosystem in Cambodia.

In August 2026, Jim Baldy, Senior Investment Associate at CIFC, spoke at the Plug and Play APAC Community Series. His panel, “Bridging the AI Hype and the Founder-Investor Reality”, looked at investment discipline, how founders and investors can stay aligned, and what strategic guidance can add beyond capital.

Prior to the signing of the MOU, Canadia Impact Fund (CIFC) and Plug and Play had already established an investment partnership through their co-investment in Cambodian EdTech startup Bamnang, reflecting their shared commitment to supporting young promising founders.

Thierry Tea said: “In our vision to push the limits and move the lines of innovation investment landscape in Cambodia, we need to build the best talents. In order to succeed in this mission, we have to collaborate with all like minded experts in international tech investments. Entering into a partnership with Plug N Play is the beginning of our learning journey to reach the same level as the best Venture Capital institutions in the world. We are aware that the road ahead is quite long, but we are strongly committed to continue our progress step by step along the growth of the local ecosystem.”

The MoU now turns this strengthened relationship into a more formalized partnership. CIFC and Plug and Play APAC plan to work together on start-up acceleration, mentoring, investor engagement and knowledge sharing, so that Cambodian founders can learn from peers abroad, meet the right people and reach new markets.

Launched in October 2025, Canadia Impact Fund in its first year of operations has invested in tech startups from 4 different countries, including Singapore, Philippines, Cambodia and France covering PropTech, EdTech, Logistics, AI, Software Development and Blockchain solutions.

As Cambodia’s start-up scene grows, Canadia Impact Fund sees international links as a way to help local companies compete beyond the country’s borders.

Canadia Impact Fund backs 2 technology startups Choose & Connect, DOCONCHAIN at FrancoTech

item.title: YTL Power denies Johor’s data center assisted transfer of NVIDIA GPUs to Chinese clients
item.dc:creator: Yimie Yong
item.description: "Various press reports have appeared linking YTL to the current controversy surrounding NVIDIA, some even implying that the YTL data centers have in some way assisted in the transfer of Nvidia GPUs to Chinese customers. These speculative and unsubstantiated reports are completely untrue," the company said in a statement on Friday.
item.content:encoded:
Malaysia-based YTL Power International Bhd has denied allegations that its data centers in Johor were involved in diverting Nvidia chips to Chinese customers.

“Various press reports have appeared linking YTL to the current controversy surrounding NVIDIA, some even implying that the YTL data centers have in some way assisted in the transfer of Nvidia GPUs to Chinese customers. These speculative and unsubstantiated reports are completely untrue,” the company said in a statement on Friday.

YTL Power said YTL Data Centers provides co-location services (space, power, cooling and connectivity) in Johor to multiple global customers, including hyperscalers from the US, under arrangements that are compliant to both local laws and U.S. trade controls.

“YTL has worked closely with the Malaysian Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (MITI) on its data centre developments and complied with all applicable reporting and import requirements,” the company said.

YTL Power’s statement came after The New York Times on Thursday reported that YTL Power’s Johor data center was allegedly used by Chinese technology giant Alibaba to remotely access NVIDIA chips through Singapore-based Megaspeed and its Malaysian subsidiary, Speedmatrix.

According to YTL Power, the new interim final rule (Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors) issued by the US Department of Commerce Bureau of Industry and Security does not affect YTL’s co-location services as the rule focuses on importers of GPUs and providers of computing services to D:5 customers.

“We remain confident that the demand for co-location data center infrastructure in Malaysia will continue to grow given strong global demand, including from the US,” the company said.

item.title: Fujitsu and Paradigm test AI screening for Japan trials
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: Fujitsu, a Japanese cancer center and Paradigm used AI to narrow clinical-trial candidates and reduce records requiring manual review by 89 percent.
item.content:encoded:
Fujitsu Japan, the National Cancer Center Hospital East and US-based Paradigm Health have tested an AI-assisted system for identifying potential participants in clinical trials in Japan.

The partners used a large language model to structure patient information from electronic medical records and linked the resulting data to Paradigm’s clinical trial matching platform, according to a Fujitsu Japan statement on Thursday.

The retrospective verification study covered records from 22,334 patients in the hospital’s respiratory medicine department between June and the end of October. For a simulated trial involving EGFR gene mutations, Fujitsu processed data from 3,027 lung-cancer patients and identified 540 records with the mutation for evaluation against five eligibility criteria.

Paradigm’s platform selected 57 priority candidates and presented clinical evidence supporting those selections. Physicians subsequently reviewed the records and determined that 51 were promising candidates, Fujitsu said.

The study also found that automated overnight processing reduced the number of records requiring manual review by approximately 89 percent. The partners said the approach could help medical staff apply standardized criteria without manually searching dispersed treatment histories, test results and genomic information.

Fujitsu stressed that the output did not determine whether patients were eligible for a real trial. Final eligibility would remain subject to trial requirements, physician review and patient consent.

The work addresses a recruitment challenge in Japan, where increasingly specific genetic and biomarker criteria can make it difficult for clinical staff to identify eligible patients. Fujitsu has also framed the project as part of efforts to reduce “drug loss,” a term used for treatments available overseas that are not developed or approved in Japan.

The company plans to commercialize a service supporting the process from candidate screening through clinical trial enrollment by the end of fiscal 2027. It said the partners intend to promote adoption by medical institutions across Japan.

Paradigm separately reported preliminary findings from the research at the European Society for Medical Oncology Congress in October. The November announcement adds Fujitsu’s detailed workflow, physician-review results and commercialization target.

Fujitsu tackles ‘drug loss’ in Japan through ecosystem to accelerate digitalization of clinical trials

item.title: MetaComp adds about $10M from Tether and Further
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: Singapore payments company MetaComp has added about $10 million from Tether and Further, bringing its Pre-A financing to roughly $45 million.
item.content:encoded:
Singapore-headquartered payments company MetaComp has extended its Pre-A+ financing with an investment of approximately $10 million from stablecoin issuer Tether and Abu Dhabi-based Further Asset Management.

The transaction brings MetaComp’s Pre-A and Pre-A+ financing to about $45 million, including a $35 million round completed in March 2026, the company said in a statement on Thursday.

MetaComp said it will use the new capital to strengthen regulatory and compliance capabilities and develop additional payment channels in priority markets. The company is targeting payment corridors linking Asia with the Middle East and Africa, where it serves financial institutions and businesses moving funds across fiat and stablecoin rails.

The Singapore company is licensed by the Monetary Authority of Singapore as a Major Payment Institution. It said its platform connects with more than 60 financial institutions and more than 170 payment service providers, supports 60 currencies across fiat and stablecoins, and processes more than $1 billion in monthly volume.

Those operating figures, including more than 1,000 institutional clients and assets under management exceeding $600 million, were supplied by MetaComp and were stated as accurate as of October 30.

Tether Chief Executive Paolo Ardoino said the investment reflects the company’s focus on regulated stablecoin infrastructure in emerging-market trade corridors. Further, an investment platform focused on financial infrastructure and digital assets, is expected to support MetaComp’s expansion and institutional relationships in the Middle East.

The financing follows MetaComp’s expansion of the StableX Agentic Network, which is designed to route transactions across traditional banking and stablecoin rails. MetaComp said the network has grown to more than 1,000 members reaching more than 100,000 users since its launch in November 2025.

The company also operates compliance tools for transactions initiated by artificial intelligence agents. Its Know-Your-Agent framework governs network admission, while its VisionX system monitors fiat and blockchain activity, according to the announcement.

MetaComp said its March financing was backed by investors including Alibaba, Eastern Bell Capital, Noah, Sky9 Capital and Spark Venture. It did not disclose the valuation or the individual amounts invested by Tether and Further in the extension.

MetaComp scales interoperable payment network to advance cross-border payments in ASEAN
